pillar_reactions.evidence: Asked how the programming worked — 'so it's built off of like an incremental, like, hey, okay, do this and regain control of your body and build it back stronger' — and later 'what does starting the program look like...the routines get kind of custom tailored to your lifestyle or your physique and your goals.' Understood it and probed mechanics; also volunteered his own shoulder weakness as something the program would need to account for.

Rep tied it back to the prospect's own 'one week on, three weeks off' admission and explained the no-macro-tracking approach. Prospect responded 'Yes, it does' to the comprehension check and offered a side comment about Philadelphia food. No questions, no pushback.

Volunteered a positive reaction to the no-subscription framing — 'That's a beautiful business model. Yeah. I like it' — and immediately tied it to his own goal: 'something I'm trying to build something that is just non-negotiable...do it every day.' This was the pillar that landed hardest and it maps directly onto the gap he named.

anchors.raw: that could definitely be a one-year membership at a nice country club. Like, well, I mean, then I could walk a course every day and maybe get, you know, the same level of movement for that same price
anchors.note: The prospect priced $6,000 against a full year of golf club access and judged the movement benefit comparable. Golf is his stated hobby goal, so this is not an idle comparison — it is a competing use of the same budget that also serves the same goal. The rep never contested it.

anchors.raw: I was looking at, like, maybe... Higher quality, maybe gym membership pricing, but $1,000 a month is pretty steep.
anchors.note: Anchored at premium-gym monthly pricing, roughly an order of magnitude below the offer. Set before the call by whatever the setter or the marketing implied; nothing in the call reset it before the number was said.

anchors.raw: I'm going to continue, I guess, learning off YouTube and saving the videos on Instagram and try it my way
anchors.note: A zero-cost substitute he already uses and has already failed with for ten years by his own account. Strong anchor precisely because it feels free; the rep had the prospect's own admission that this exact behaviour is the failure pattern and never used it.

anchors.raw: I did do a kettlebell class...And then I looked at the price tag of what it would be every week, I was like, ooh, okay, I'll try to figure that out on my own.
anchors.note: Established a personal precedent of walking away from coaching on price. A per-week class rate is the reference frame he brought to a $6,000 lump sum.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching at roughly premium-gym-membership pricing — he named around $1,000/month as already steep and had $1,500 in savings against ~$3-5k cash
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The lowest published tier is $6,000 for six months. The rep improvised a $4,000 / 3-month option at ~$400 per month, still roughly double what the prospect described as feasible, and there is no entry-level or lower-touch product beneath it.

unmet_demand.want: Training that works around and does not aggravate a 20-year ankle injury with a suspected bone cyst, MRI pending and possible surgery in the near term
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted the mobility programme would be 'alleviating any limitations' and made it a selling point, but nobody established whether loaded ballistic kettlebell work is safe or appropriate pre- or post-ankle surgery, and no clinician input was sought or referenced.
